newsitem.title: USA: TCI preliminary Q1 revs, cash flow up.
newsitem.headline: TCI preliminary Q1 revs, cash flow up.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc said Tuesday that preliminary first quarter, unadjusted revenues for its cable operations were $1.556 billion, compared to $1.333 billion for the 1996 quarter.
The company said operating cash flow results for its domestic cable operations were $701 million, compared to cash flow of $498 million for the 1996 period.

Adjusting for acquisitions and dispositions on a proforma basis, revenues in the first quarter 1997 were $1.562 billion and operating cash flow was $704 million, including financial results for TKR Cable for the 10 days before its acquisition, TCI said.
The company said its proforma revenues in the year-ago quarter were $1.433 billion and its proforma operating cash flow was $569 million.
The cable giant also said it plans to roll out a basic digital product to 75 to 90 percent of its homes passed by the end of 1997, assuming vendors meet specified timetables.
It said that beginning in May, it would launch its basic digital product with an additional 40 video channels and 14 audio channels.
It would fund said the upgrade and roll-out of digital TV with internally generated funds.
TCI also said the numbers of its basic and pay subscribers fell since December 31, excluding the effect of acquisitions, and attributed the drops to rate increases.

Excluding the effect of acquisitions, the number of basic cable customers fell by 83,000 from 13.9 million in December of 1996, and the number of pay subscriptions fell by more than one million from 15 million, it said.

"The company largely attributes its basic customer and pay subscription declines to recently implemented rate increases made necessary in large part by significant increases in programming costs," the company said in a release. "Despite these basic customer and pay subscription decines, revenue and cash flow were positively impacted by the pricing adjustements."

Including the effect of acquisitions, cable operations ended the first quarter with 14.370 million basic cable customers, a three percent increase from the number at the period ended December 31, 1996, TCI said.
The company said preliminary debt balance for its cable operations at the end of the first quarter was $14.480 billion, including $574 million of debt related to the TKR acquisition.
